From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: bassê, Bässe, and Basse

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

basse

  1. Archaic form of bass (“perch”).
  2. (music jargon) The bass voice or part within French music

See also

[edit]
  • basse court
  • basse-taille

Anagrams

[edit]
  • bases, bessa

Danish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse bassi (“bear”).

Noun

[edit]

basse c (singular definite bassen, plural indefinite basser)

  1. a big, strong man, a big thing
  2. an army infantryman, a private
  3. a Danish pastry

Inflection

[edit]
Declension of basse
common
gender 		singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative basse bassen basser basserne
genitive basses bassens bassers bassernes

Derived terms

[edit]
  • brumbasse

basse

  1. (dated or formal) singular present subjunctive of bassen

French

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bas/ ~ /bɑs/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Canada (Shawinigan)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Adjective

[edit]

basse

  1. feminine singular of bas

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian basso; homophony with Etymology 1 led to reinterpretation as a feminine, specifically as an ellipsis of la voix basse (“the low voice”).

Noun

[edit]

basse f (plural basses)

  1. (music) bass (the lower melody)
  2. (music) bass (a singer of the bass melodies)
  3. (music) bass (the musical instrument)
  4. acoustic guitar
Derived terms
[edit]
  • basse continue
  • contrebasse
  • bassiste
  • guitare basse

Further reading

[edit]
  • “basse”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • bases, basés

Interlingua

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

basse (comparative plus basse, superlative le plus basse)

  1. low

Antonyms

[edit]
  • alte

Norwegian Bokmål

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse bassi (“bear”).

Noun

[edit]

basse m (definite singular bassen, indefinite plural basser, definite plural bassene)

  1. a big, strong man
  2. (especially in compounds) an unruly man

Derived terms

[edit]
  • brumlebasse
  • spradebasse
  • villbasse

References

[edit]
  • “basse” in The Bokmål Dictionary.

Norwegian Nynorsk

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • (Aasen): Basse (obsolete capitalization)[1]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse bassi (“bear”).[2]

Noun

[edit]

basse m (definite singular bassen, indefinite plural bassar, definite plural bassane)

  1. a big, strong man
  2. (especially in compounds) an unruly man
  3. (Setesdal, Telemark) synonym of bamse (“bear”)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • brumlebasse
  • spradebasse
  • villbasse

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Ivar Aasen (1850), “Basse”, in Ordbog over det norske Folkesprog‎[1] (in Danish), Oslo: Samlaget, published 2000
  2. ^ “basse” in The Nynorsk Dictionary.
